search_text: published ZDI-24-499 ZDI-CAN-22446 (Pwn2Own) TP-Link Omada ER605 PPTP VPN username Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability 2024-05-23 CVE-2024-5227 https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2024-5227 7.5 AV:A/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H ['TP-Link'] ['Omada ER605'] This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of TP-Link Omada ER605 routers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. However, devices are only vulnerable if configured to use a PPTP VPN with LDAP authentication. The specific flaw exists within the handling of the username parameter provided to the /usr/bin/pppd endpoint. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of root. Fixed in firmware ER605 (UN) _V2_2. 2.4 Build 20240119 https://www.tp-link.com/en/support/download/er605/#Firmware ['2023-11-09 - Vulnerability reported to vendor', '2024-05-23 - Coordinated public release of advisory', '2024-07-01 - Advisory Updated'] Chris Anastasio @mufinnnnnnn https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-24-499/
title: (Pwn2Own) TP-Link Omada ER605 PPTP VPN username Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
vulnerability_details: This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of TP-Link Omada ER605 routers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. However, devices are only vulnerable if configured to use a PPTP VPN with LDAP authentication. The specific flaw exists within the handling of the username parameter provided to the /usr/bin/pppd endpoint. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of root.
